key_insight: A dual-scale deep learning framework that combines 10x and 20x histopathology views, plus clinical metadata, can improve automated detection and staging support for mycosis fungoides.
clinical_relevance: The approach is aimed at helping clinicians distinguish early mycosis fungoides from benign inflammatory skin disease and support later staging decisions in confirmed cases.
method: Late-fusion ensemble of CNNs using 10x and 20x histopathology images
Random forest model trained on 16 clinical features
Separate models for screening (MF vs non-MF) and staging (patch/plaque vs tumor)
evidence_signal: The study evaluated 6,267 images from 463 patients and reported 83.58% accuracy/89.13% sensitivity for the image-based model and 96.6% accuracy/93.8% sensitivity for the clinical random forest model.
watch_item: Performance may depend on dataset size, class balance, and local pathology practices, so external validation is needed before routine deployment.
paper_title: Detail in Context: A Dual-Scale Machine Learning Framework for Mycosis Fungoides Detection
